names: P10 -- landscaped center island, Mission Bay Circle roundabout
summary: The landscaped center island (grass, trees) of the 'Mission Bay Circle' roundabout in Mission Bay, where Mission Bay Drive, Owens, Channel and Mission Bay Boulevard meet; a real, already-built park feature distinct from the surrounding road pavement, per satellite imagery and this project's owner-guided tracing. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P10' among the parcels already managed by SF Recreation and Parks (not among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), consistent with it being complete by that date.

milestones.text: EPA Region 9 / California DTSC $760,000 Revolving Loan Fund hazardous-substances subgrant funds construction of "Mission Bay Park P10" together with Mission Bay Circle -- soil removal/relocation, clean fill import, a landscape/hardscape cap and a methane mitigation system; construction projected to employ approximately 395 workers over 15 months

Mission Bay Circle (the roundabout containing this island) shown to a DTSC/EPA/City press tour as a "landscaped turnaround that will eventually serve as a gateway to the park corridor" -- described in future tense, i.e. not yet functional at this date

Already part of RPD's managed open-space inventory (not listed among the still-pending 'when built' parcels), per OCII's Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation to the Mission Bay CAC -- an upper bound on when this island was built, not its actual construction date

sources.title: Mission Bay Parks Open Space (CAC Item 2, September 2023)
sources.publisher: Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (sfocii.org)

sources.title: Brownfields Program Revolving Loan Fund (RLF) Success Stories -- California DTSC Subgrants fact sheet (Subgrant 4: "Mission Bay Park P10")

open_questions: 2026-09-22 pass: a 2011-2012-era EPA/DTSC brownfields fact sheet directly names "Mission Bay Park P10" (Subgrant 4, $760,000) funding its construction together with Mission Bay Circle, and a Nov 2011 press-tour article shows the Circle still not yet functional at that date -- but neither source gives an exact construction-start date, only that funded work was under way by 2010-2011. The original park/roundabout's exact start and completion dates remain unconfirmed.
Owner/operator beyond 'part of RPD's Mission Bay open-space inventory' not confirmed by any source found.
